Lessons.Title: Derivatives
ExplanationParagraphs: Derivative f'(a)=lim_(h→0)[f(a+h)−f(a)]/h when finite limit exists.
Power rule (x^n)'=n x^(n−1) and linearity differentiate polynomials.
Differentiate reciprocal and radical functions within their smooth domains.
Derivative is instantaneous rate; average rate is secant slope.
A corner or jump can prevent differentiability; differentiability implies continuity.
Tangent line y−f(a)=f'(a)(x−a); applied derivatives include marginal cost and velocity.
Independent Cool-down: evaluate a representative local example and explain the limiting or derivative reasoning.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Substitute directly into0/0 or assume a hole changes approached limit.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Limit concerns nearby behavior, not isolated point value.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Accepting an answer without validating the original problem conditions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An algebraic candidate can violate a given domain, interval, sign, model assumption or unit restriction.
